1) Can production data (messages, embeddings, logs, backups, and audit trails) be guaranteed to remain only in EU regions (no backups or analytics leaving EU) when we use Redwood Private (VPC)?

4) Are there any cross-tenant caches or services that could cause inadvertent data residency leakage?
5) Please reference the latest SOC 2 report and a completed SIG (or CAIQ) matrix if available.

We'd like to include your responses in our formal SIG import and to share a summary with our auditors. If you prefer, a short attestation email and redacted SOC2 PDF would be sufficient for now.

Hi Tom / Neha — following up with the technical details you requested. Long-ish but I wanted to be specific so your auditors can map controls.

Short answers up front:
- Yes — with Redwood Private deployed into your EU VPC/region, production data (user content, embeddings, logs, snapshots, and audit events) can be restricted to EU regions only. Cross-region replication is disabled by default and only enabled with explicit customer request and sign-off.
- Yes — we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For HSM-backed keys we support AWS CloudHSM integrations for dedicated deployments.
- No cross-tenant data leakage: our serving runtime isolates KV caches per tenant; shared services (control plane) only hold metadata pointers, not customer content.

More detail:
1) Data residency (production and backups)
- Persistent storage for Private deployments is provisioned in the customer-designated region (e.g., eu-west-1). Backups/snapshots are stored in the same region by default.
- Analytics pipelines are opt-in and run in customer-controlled VPCs or in the same region; we do not ship raw customer data to external analytics by default.
- Audit logs: retained per your retention policy; log storage location equals the deployment region unless you request exports.

2) KMS / encryption
- Supported: AWS KMS (symmetric + customer-managed CMKs), GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault.
- HSM: AWS CloudHSM support for dedicated clusters.
- Integration timeline: standard integration (bring your key, provide IAM/KMS permissions) takes 3–10 business days for key provisioning and validation; full production integration (end-to-end testing + rotate keys) typically 2–4 weeks depending on customer IAM reviews.

3) Network topology / VPC controls
- We provide a VPC runbook that includes: private endpoint setup, VPC peering/Transit Gateway patterns, recommended security groups, subnet slicing for isolate control plane traffic, and NAT/egress gateway configuration to enforce EU-only egress.
- Private DNS and no-public-internet modes are supported.

4) Caching / shared services
- KV caches are allocated per tenant and never shared across customer boundaries. We do not colocate customer caches with other tenants in Private deployments.

Attachments included with this message (stubs):
- redwood-soc2-report-2025-redacted.pdf (redacted SOC 2 Type II report)
- redwood-sig-matrix-2025.xlsx (SIG/CAIQ answers matrix)
- vpc-onprem-runbook.pdf (VPC topology and provisioning steps)

If you prefer, we can fill your SIG import sheet directly — share the URL/CSV and we'll return answers in the format your tool expects.

Timeline expectation for a standard Private deployment to EU (approx):
- Week 0–1: legal & onboarding, KMS access provisioning
- Week 1–2: infra provision (VPC, subnets, Bastion/priv-endpoints)
- Week 2–4: model & data migration, validation, and QA
Total: typically 3–6 weeks depending on procurement and IAM approvals.
